title: Intense pulsed light (IPL)
summary: Counselling on intense pulsed light for redness, pigment and hair: who is a good candidate, what to expect, and the burn and pigment risks, especially in tanned or darker skin.

what: **Intense pulsed light (IPL)** is a non-laser flashlamp delivering broad-spectrum light through filters to treat vascular redness, solar lentigines and unwanted dark hair, with modest texture benefit.

list: Selective photothermolysis: melanin and oxyhaemoglobin absorb the light and heat up; dermal heating may remodel collagen modestly.
Darker or tanned skin absorbs more epidermal energy, giving a higher risk of burns and pigment change.
Sessions often 3–6, weeks apart; treated pigment darkens like “coffee grounds” then flakes over 1–2 weeks.
Adverse effects: burns, blistering, **hypo-/hyperpigmentation** (sometimes grid footprints), scarring, paradoxical hair growth, eye injury.

diagnosis: Before IPL: confirm the diagnosis of every pigmented spot (no undiagnosed lesions), Fitzpatrick type, recent tan, photosensitising drugs and HSV history. Melasma is generally a poor IPL candidate.

head: Request
Better framed as
rows: IPL photofacial after a skin cancer check
Often a pigment laser rather than IPL
Sunscreen + medical therapy; avoid heat devices first-line (see [Melasma](condition:melasma-facial-melanosis))

list: Check practitioner training, insurance, patch test and (in Wales) HIW registration for Class 3B/4 lasers/IPL in independent clinics.

Contraindications/cautions: undiagnosed pigmented lesions, active infection/HSV, recent tan, photosensitivity disorders, many photosensitising drugs; extra caution in skin types IV–VI and on isotretinoin (many delay treatment).
Aftercare: SPF, gentle skincare, no picking; seek review for blistering or infection.

red_flags: Eye pain or visual change during/after IPL: **urgent ophthalmology**.
Blistering burns or striped hypopigmentation: stop further treatment; specialist wound/pigment advice.
Undiagnosed changing pigmented lesion: cancel IPL; refer.
pearls: IPL is versatile but unforgiving on tanned or darker skin without expert settings.
Coffee-ground darkening is expected; picking prolongs marks.
